body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

The initial vector is a float tensor containing NaN. After I convert it to int32 using `torch.Tensor.to`, it should still be NaN. I get the correct result on CPU, but on the GPU, I get 0.

For the code on CPU:
```
input_data = torch.tensor([float('nan')])
different_input = input_data.to(dtype=torch.int32)
print(different_input)
```
,we get the right result:
```
tensor([-2147483648], dtype=torch.int32)
```

For the code on GPU:
```
input_data = torch.tensor([float('nan')]).cuda()
different_input = input_data.to(dtype=torch.int32)
print(different_input)
```
,we get the wrong result:
```
tensor([0], device='cuda:0', dtype=torch.int32)
```

### Versions

Versions of relevant libraries:
[pip3] numpy==1.24.4
[pip3] torch==2.2.1
[pip3] triton==2.2.0
[conda] numpy 1.24.4 pypi_0 pypi
[conda] torch 2.2.1 pypi_0 pypi
[conda] triton 2.2.0 pypi_0 pypi

cc @malfet @albanD
title: input_data.to produce inconsistent results
